title: Volatility Hidden Markov Model
summary: A hidden Markov model inferring the latent volatility regime (two-state) from FTSE 100 daily returns, implemented from scratch in NumPy with out-of-sample evaluation.

title: Honeydew
summary: An open-source, local-first macOS learning agent that aims to turn useful information from your screen into Anki flashcards and short coding exercises.
problem: Knowledge encountered while working with AI assistants, reading documentation and learning new concepts is easily forgotten.
approach: Planned: on-device screen observation using macOS APIs, a local language model for topic-aware flashcard generation, and daily CSV export for Anki.
results: The command-line foundation is implemented. Screen observation, local inference and Anki export are planned but not yet available.

title: PhD Exchange
summary: Knowledge exchange for researchers: a place for PhD students, postdocs and academics to meet, share their interests and learn about each other’s work outside their own field.

title: Wavelet Spectral Features for Financial Shocks
summary: Investigating whether wavelet-based spectral features characterise financial shocks and improve out-of-sample volatility forecasts.
approach: Causal wavelet decomposition (MODWT) of return series, with relative band shares of local wavelet power as features.
Evaluated against standard volatility baselines, including HAR-RV and GARCH models.

title: Hidden Markov Models of Bowler Strategy
summary: A hidden Markov model of bowler strategy and fatigue, used to classify play into phases of building and releasing pressure on the batter.
problem: Bowler strategy and fatigue are not directly observed, but they shape the sequence of deliveries. The partner needed a way to infer these hidden states from the delivery sequence.
approach: Formulated bowler strategy and fatigue as hidden states in a hidden Markov model.
Inferred the most likely state sequence with the Viterbi algorithm, implemented in Python.
results: Classified play into phases of building and releasing pressure on the batter, approved by expert review.
confidentialNote: Partner data, reports and detailed results are proprietary and are not published here.

title: Stochastic Model of Macular Degeneration
summary: An improved cellular automaton model of disease progression that matches observed degeneration patterns.
problem: The team needed a stochastic model of disease progression that could be calibrated against observed degeneration patterns.
approach: Improved a stochastic model of disease progression within an interdisciplinary team, in the form of a cellular automaton.
Simulated the model in Python and calibrated its parameters with macular degeneration researchers.
results: An improved cellular automaton whose simulated degeneration patterns match those observed.
Co-authored a paper on the model, which has been submitted.
confidentialNote: Partner data, reports and detailed results are proprietary and are not published here.

title: Plasmid Similarity Networks
context: Department of Biology, University of Bath
summary: Random graph models of plasmid similarity, as an alternative to hard-threshold network methods.
problem: Current methods that link plasmid genomes into similarity networks rely on hard thresholds, which are subjective. The department wanted a less subjective alternative.
approach: Measured distances between plasmid genomes using three-dimensional chaos game representations.
Modelled similarity networks with random graph models in Python.
results: Random graph models offer an alternative to hard-threshold methods for building plasmid similarity networks.
The trade-off is greater variance in the resulting networks than with thresholding.
confidentialNote: Partner data, reports and detailed results are proprietary and are not published here.
